output.brief: The rejections were most likely caused by a data error in the new documentation system. The mandarin product record was copied from avocado on 1 Aug, and its carriage temperature was left at 7.0°C. The specification is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through the new system was sent at 7.0°C, and every one was rejected. The container controllers held that setpoint, within 0.4°C. The Coastway and early Meridane containers were set at 4.0°C and passed. Two of the rejected containers (K3, K4) were on 7.0°C even though K3 used old fungicide, and Pellacor fruit at 4.0°C passed. That counts against the fungicide theory. Meridane followed our instructions, so a claim against them would likely fail. Suspending Lower Serra is not justified. Their fruit was worse within rejected containers, but I can't tell whether that is a real effect or only a result of the temperature error. What to do now: correct the product record to 4.0°C. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check comparing reefer settings with the product specification before bookings go out. Hold off on the claim, the suspension and the fungicide switch. Independent loggers are optional. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
